transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you’re here. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, uh, I hope I'm not wasting your time today or taking up a spot from someone who really needs it. 

I guess what brings me in is... well, since I stopped working, I just can't seem to slow down. I mean, I know it's a good thing to stay active, right? But I'm just constantly up and moving from one little job around the house to the next, all day long. It's almost like I still have a work crew waiting on me to get things moving. 

It's probably nothing to make a big fuss over, but my family mentioned it, so I figured I should ask. Is that the sort of thing you handle here? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual and still feeling energized?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I definitely still need my sleep. I mean, I hope that's okay to say, but I'm not... I don't think I'm running on empty and feeling great about it or anything. 

When I'm up all day doing those little jobs, by the time evening rolls around, I'm pretty worn out, just like anyone my age would be. I usually get my regular hours in at night. Is that what you mean? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. I don't want to make it sound like I'm doing anything too unusual at night.
During this time, have you felt unusually high, overly cheerful, or more irritable than usual?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I hope I'm not coming across as grumpy or anything today. I try my best to keep a positive attitude, you know? 

I haven't felt unusually high or overly cheerful, either. Just... normal, I guess? I mean, I might get a little frustrated if I misplace my reading glasses or something small like that, but I wouldn't say I'm more irritable than usual. I really try not to be a bother to anyone. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things have been.
Have you ever had a period when you felt much more energetic or active than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've always been a bit of a busybody, you know? But I wouldn't say there was ever a time where I was just... bouncing off the walls or anything like that. 

I just like to keep moving, keep busy. I hope that's alright to say. I don't want to make it sound like I'm doing something wrong by staying active. I just... I haven't noticed any big changes in my energy levels, just the usual day-to-day stuff. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I just want to be sure I'm answering you properly.
Have your thoughts been racing unusually fast?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean... sometimes I'll be thinking about a few chores I need to get to, just normal everyday stuff, but my mind isn't... it's not racing or going unusually fast. I try to keep a pretty level head about things. 

I hope that makes sense? I just wouldn't want you to think my brain is spinning out of control or anything, because it really isn't. I just take things one step at a time. Am I explaining that okay for you? I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Have you been talking more than usual or finding it hard to stop talking?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think I've been talking too much. I mean, I enjoy a nice chat with the neighbors or the cashier at the grocery store, just being polite, you know? But I certainly wouldn't say I can't stop talking or that I'm talking anyone's ear off. 

I really try to be mindful of other people's time and make sure I'm listening just as much as I'm speaking. I wouldn't want to be a nuisance or come across as overbearing. I hope I haven't been talking too much today? I just want to make sure I'm answering all your questions the way you need me to.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Well, I suppose... maybe just a little bit? Nothing too terrible, I promise. It's just that, well, sometimes if I'm trying to do something nice, like maybe painting a little or trying to plan out a story to write, my mind sort of... wanders off. 

Like, if I hear a delivery truck rumbling by outside, or if I suddenly remember a weed I meant to pull in the garden, my thoughts just jump right over to that instead. And then I sort of lose my place with what I was doing. It's just normal getting-older stuff, right? I try really hard to stay focused, I do. I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or not trying hard enough. Does that sound like what you're asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Have you been noticing problems with your memory?

Well, maybe just a little bit, but nothing to worry about, really. I mean, at my age, you expect a few slips here and there, right? 

Lately, I suppose I've been... well, forgetting a few little things. Like returning a call from the folks down at the community center, or... occasionally I might forget to pay a bill right on time until my wife gently reminds me. And the other day, I was supposed to bring some supplies for my garden group and it completely slipped my mind. 

I felt just awful about it, I really did. I always try to be dependable. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely scatterbrained? I'm really trying my best to keep on top of things. Is that the kind of memory stuff you were wondering about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you helpful answers.
Have these memory or concentration problems started to interfere with your day-to-day activities, like managing bills, medications, or getting things done around the house?

Well, I wouldn't say "interfere," exactly. That sounds so... serious. I'm still getting by just fine, really. But, well, my wife... she's such a dear, she's started keeping the calendar for us. Just to, you know, check behind me and make sure everything is squared away. She says it's no trouble at all. 

And I suppose... well, I have had to apologize to the folks at the community center and the garden group a couple of times lately. Just for silly little mix-ups, letting them down when I didn't mean to. I hate being a bother to anyone, I truly do. I always try to be the one helping out, not the one causing extra work. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a burden? We just lean on each other a bit more these days, my wife and I. Does that answer your question all right? I want to make sure I'm explaining things clearly for you.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot more than is typical for you?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I try to be a pretty cheerful fellow, really. I mean, sure, everyone has a little fret now and then—maybe about the grandkids or, you know, just the price of groceries these days—but nothing out of the ordinary, I promise. 

I certainly don't want you to think I'm sitting around wringing my hands all day! I really try to just look on the bright side of things and take each day as it comes. Is... is it alright that I don't have much to report on that front? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you find it hard to control your worrying?

Oh, no, not at all. Like I was saying, I really don't consider myself a worrier. I mean, if a little concern pops up, I just kind of brush it off and move on to something else, you know? 

I certainly don't feel like my thoughts are running away with me or anything like that. I'm usually pretty good at just... letting things go. I hope that's a good thing? I really try to be easygoing and not let things get under my skin. I'm doing okay with these questions, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you worry that your memory problems mean something serious is wrong with your mind?

Oh, goodness, no. I mean, sure, nobody likes forgetting things, but I don't jump to any scary conclusions like that. I figure it's just a normal part of getting a little older, isn't it? Just the usual wear and tear, nothing to make a big fuss over. 

I certainly don't sit around thinking I'm losing my mind or anything awful like that. I just try to laugh it off when I misplace my keys or forget a name. It's better to keep a sense of humor about these things, don't you think? I hope I'm not sounding too... dismissive? I just really don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill. Does that make sense to you?
Have these memory and concentration changes been getting worse over time?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say they're getting worse. I mean, it's just the same old me, really. A little scatterbrained sometimes, sure, but it's not like it's a downward spiral or anything dramatic like that. 

I think it's just... well, it's just how I've always been, and maybe I just notice it a bit more now that I have more time on my hands since I retired. But I certainly don't feel like I'm slipping away or anything. I'm still keeping up with things just fine. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to be sure I'm giving you an accurate picture without making it sound worse than it is.
Have you had any trouble managing your medications on your own?

Oh, no, managing my medications is no trouble at all. I've got a pretty good system going. I mean, maybe I'm a few hours late taking a pill here or there if I get distracted doing something around the house, but I always get to it eventually. 

It's nothing I can't handle, really. I just keep them right on the kitchen counter where I can see them. I don't need any special help with it or anything like that. I'm doing all right with that, aren't I? I mean, a little slip-up now and then is pretty normal, wouldn't you say? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing.
Do you ever forget important recent events, like conversations you had earlier the same day?

Oh, goodness, no, nothing like that. I mean, sure, sometimes my wife will say, "I told you that this morning," and I might not remember it right away, but... well, usually if she gives me a little hint, it comes right back to me. 

It's not like I'm just wiping the slate clean every few hours! I think sometimes I'm just... you know, my mind is on other things, maybe tinkering in the garage or watching a game, and I just don't file the conversation away properly. But I don't think I'm really *forgetting* important things. That sounds okay, right? I mean, husbands not listening to their wives is practically a cliché, isn't it? I hope that doesn't sound too bad.
Have these memory and concentration problems been getting worse over time?

Oh... well, like I think I mentioned just a little bit ago—and I'm so sorry if I didn't explain it clearly enough the first time—but no, I really wouldn't say they're getting worse at all. It's just my usual way of being, you know? 

There's been no sudden drop-off or anything alarming like that. I hope it's alright that my answer is still the same? I just really don't feel like there's been any sort of real decline, honestly. I think I'm doing pretty well for my age, all things considered. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Have you had any weakness or numbness on one side of your body?

Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like that at all. I haven't had any... well, no weakness or numbness anywhere. Both sides are working just fine, thankfully. 

I mean, I try to keep moving around the house and stay in decent shape for my age. That's a good sign, isn't it? I certainly hope so. I just want to make sure I'm doing okay and giving you the right information. But no, physically, everything is perfectly fine in that department, I promise.
Have you ever had a stroke or other sudden neurologic event in the past?

Oh, heavens, no. No strokes or... or any sudden neurological things like that. Thank goodness, right? I've been very blessed in that department. 

I mean, I try to take care of myself as best I can, so... well, I hope that's reassuring to hear? I always feel a little bad just saying 'no' over and over, like I'm not giving you enough information to go on, but I really haven't had anything scary like that happen. My health is pretty sturdy overall. I hope I'm still doing okay with answering your questions?
Have you started needing help with things you used to do entirely on your own, like handling your finances?

Oh... well, with the finances, I think I'm still doing alright there. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I hope this doesn't sound too terrible—I have needed a little bit of help with a few other things. 

My wife, bless her, she's sort of had to take over keeping the calendar and... well, just checking behind me sometimes to make sure things get done. It's really just a little extra teamwork, I think! Nothing too serious. Though, um... it is a little embarrassing to admit, but I have had to apologize to the folks at the community center and my garden group more than once lately for sort of... letting people down. Just missing things I said I'd do. I feel just awful about it, I really do, because I hate being a bother or a disappointment to anyone. 

Is that the sort of thing you mean? I hope I'm not painting too bad a picture of myself. I really am trying my very best to keep up with everything, I promise.
Do these memory and concentration problems make it hard for you to manage your own finances?

Oh, no, no, the finances are... they're really okay. I can still handle paying the bills and keeping track of the checkbook just fine. 

I mean, I might have to double-check a number here or there just to be absolutely sure, but I haven't had any real trouble with the money side of things. I'm very careful about that, I promise. I know how important it is to keep all of that straight. So, I'm still doing all of that on my own. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it alright.
